text:
maria: Quick question - eng lead changed to 0.8 FTE for 6 months (medical accomodation), then returned to 1.0 FTE. Their accruals were pro-rated during that period. They ended the year with 44 accrued hours on the system (some from before the FTE change). Manager asked whether carryover cap should be applied on FTE-normalized basis or absolute hours. Any precedent?

jon: Short answer: accruals are pro-rated by FTE during the period, but the carryover cap in policy is an absolute hours cap (40h). We’ve made exceptions before for mid-year FTE changes but those were manual approvals.

hailey: Payroll side  we need exact dates and employee id. If systems show 44h, we can split the balance by date ranges and recalc expected accrual vs recorded. Also need to know if any PTO was used while 0.8 FTE.

maria: Employee id 77219, FTE change 2025-09-01 to 2026-02-28, returned to 1.0 on 2026-03-01. No PTO used while 0.8. Manager wants to allow carryover of the full 44h because the reduction in accrual was a company-requested accommodation.

tina: People Ops POV: accommodation reason matters. If the FTE change was requested by company (not employee), granting full carryover is defensible. Proposed approach: 1) Recalculate theoretical full-time accrual for the period, 2) If theoretical > recorded, allow carryover up to theoretical but cap at 80h absolute emergency limit (we never do >40 without Director sign-off), 3) If >40, require Director approval and note accommodation on record.

legal: Quick legal flag  in some jurisdictions (e.g., NL, FR), you can't disadvantage employees for permitted medical accommodations. If the accommodation was employer-driven, we should avoid a policy outcome that reduces leave compared to what they'd have had as FT. Will confirm jurisdiction specifics once you send the country.

hailey: Payroll: If People Ops approves an exception, we need a signed approval form and then a CSV to ingest before payroll cutoff. Current cutoff: 2026-04-12 17:00 PT. CSV shape we need: employee_id,action,hours,effective_date,pay_code,reason,approval_id. Example: 

employee_id,action,hours,effective_date,pay_code,reason,approval_id
77219,carryover_add,4,2026-04-15,CARRY,accommodation-exception,APPR-2026-089

maria: Thank you. One nuance: the employee already shows 44h in system; do we need to "add" hours or mark an exception so payroll doesn't auto-payout the 4h over cap?

tina: Two options: 1) mark a policy exception on the HR record (no payroll entry) and prevent payout at termination; or 2) add the extra hours as carryover so system balance stays accurate. Option 1 is lighter technically. Suggest option 1 unless Finance needs ledger entries.

payroll-bot: payroll-bot: Note - if you use exception flag approach, include field no_payout=TRUE in request so payroll won't auto-payout at termination. If you add hours, we need GL mapping. Sample flag CSV: 

employee_id,action,adjustment_flag,no_payout,approval_id,notes
77219,flag,EXCEPTION,TRUE,APPR-2026-089,FT accommodation - prevent payout

legal: Also recommend documenting manager request and the medical accommodation rationale (high level) in the approval so audit trail is clear but keep PHI out of the record.

maria: I'll collect manager sign-off and submit the accommodation exception form today. If Director approval needed, please escalate.

tina: Great - once submitted People Ops will triage. If Director sign-off is required for >40h we'll route. Payroll will hold until CSV received before cutoff. Thanks all! :white_check_mark:
